title: Kirtar Takes the Mirari for the Order
summary: An Order officer tries to turn the Mirari into a tool of justice and demonstrates its power to corrupt good intentions.
narrative: After the sphere left Cabal custody, Lieutenant Kirtar claimed it for the Order in the hope of containing or redirecting its power.
His confidence could not overcome the Mirari's tendency to magnify the desires of its wielder. The Order's claim of righteous purpose was no guarantee of safety.
The episode preceded the sphere's passage to the cephalid empire and another disastrous attempt to control it.

The Order presented itself as a moral alternative to the Cabal's brutal entertainment economy. Yet its possession of the Mirari made the same underlying problem visible from another direction: a group could claim legitimate ends while assuming that extraordinary power would obey its intentions.

Kirtar's attempt belongs to a succession of failed claims upon the artifact. The Mirari did not require every claimant to want the same thing; it intensified each claimant's desire until private certainty created public danger. An officer seeking justice and a ruler seeking domination could therefore both contribute to the same escalating crisis.

The episode is best read as part of Otaria's wider institutional competition rather than a self-contained story of corruption. The sphere moved between organizations with different ideologies, revealing similar vulnerabilities in their leadership. Its movement also helps explain why later characters could not simply solve the conflict by placing it in another authority's hands.
